title: Isandro and the Portrait
premise: Sable Halloran, the reclusive coroner of Graywater Hollow, is paid a suspiciously generous retainer by a stranger named Isandro Vey to prove that a murder has not yet happened — a murder Isandro insists will be pinned on him. When a body surfaces matching every detail of Isandro's warning, Sable realizes the killer is someone with access to their own case files and autopsy notes. As Sable races to unmask the killer before Isandro becomes the next victim or the prime suspect, they uncover that Isandro is the long-presumed-dead son of the town's founding family, whose 'death' twenty years ago was staged to hide an earlier killing. In the end, Sable must choose between protecting Isandro's secret identity and exposing the truth: they arrest the killer — the town archivist who curated everyone's records — but at the cost of revealing Isandro alive, shattering the town's history and Sable's own carefully maintained invisibility.
about_author: Sebastian Ashgrove is the pen name of a former rural registrar who spent a decade handling death certificates in towns too small for secrets. They write mysteries about people who know too much to stay quiet and too little to feel safe.

chapters.title: The Retainer
chapters.summary: Sable Halloran's POV. A pale, precise stranger named Isandro Vey arrives at the coroner's office with a cash retainer and an impossible request: prove a murder hasn't happened yet. He names the victim, the method, even the date. Sable, unsettled but intrigued, accepts. The emotional beat is wary curiosity — Sable's pride in closing cases collides with the instinct that this client knows something terrible.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Establishing Graywater Hollow's rhythms, Sable walks the cemetery cataloguing plots and reflects on two decades of quiet deaths. A records check reveals no trace of Isandro Vey anywhere — no birth record, no tax file, nothing. The emotional beat is creeping unease: the man paying Sable to prevent a murder doesn't officially exist.

chapters.title: The Date Arrives Early
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Three days before the predicted date, a body turns up in the flooded quarry — matching Isandro's description exactly, except it isn't the person he named. The wounds match his described method precisely. Sable realizes the killer is improvising, or testing. The emotional beat is dread sharpening into resolve as Sable begins pulling old case files.

chapters.title: Files That Read Themselves
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, with a brief interlude from Deputy Cora Lin's perspective. Someone has been accessing the coroner's archived reports — pages subtly reordered, notes annotated in handwriting Sable almost recognizes. Cora notices Sable's late-night visits to the archive. The emotional beat is paranoia: the killer isn't watching the investigation; the killer is inside its paperwork.

chapters.title: What the Quarry Gave Back
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The autopsy reveals the victim was killed elsewhere and moved — and under the fingernails, fibers from a garment discontinued twenty years ago. Digging into the town's founding family, the Ashcombes, Sable finds a sealed file: the drowning death of young Isandro Ashcombe, ruled accidental, closed by Sable's own predecessor. The emotional beat is vertigo — the past reaching up through the present.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro admits he faked his death two decades ago to escape his father's cover-up of a servant girl's killing — a murder the family buried in the same archive Sable now holds. He believes the killer is finishing what the family started, eliminating witnesses. The emotional beat is raw confession and fragile trust: loyalty to a client versus duty to the truth.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Hand
chapters.summary: Cora Lin's POV. Cora, investigating the archive breaches independently, traces the annotations to Merritt Cole, the town archivist, who has quietly curated — and edited — Graywater Hollow's records for thirty years. She confronts Sable with her findings just as Merritt requests all files related to the Ashcombe estate. The emotional beat is the click of pieces aligning, shadowed by the fear of being right too late.

chapters.title: A Murder That Hasn't Happened Yet
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable stages Isandro's death using the coroner's own tools — a false report, a borrowed grave plot, misdirection in the file system — betting the killer will come to verify his work personally. The emotional beat is cold clarity: Sable weaponizes the very records the killer trusts, crossing lines they once swore never to cross.

chapters.title: Night in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Alternating Sable and Isandro POVs. Merritt Cole comes to the archive at midnight to amend one final record and finds Sable waiting; Isandro steps from the shadows as living proof of everything Merritt helped bury. Merritt confesses he killed to protect the town's curated story — and himself. A violent struggle ends with Cora arriving to make the arrest. The emotional beat is cathartic confrontation: truth dragged into the light at last.

chapters.title: Signed in Ink
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. With Merritt charged and the Ashcombe cover-up exposed, Isandro must reclaim his real name publicly — ending his invisibility and endangering the life he built. He thanks Sable and leaves Graywater Hollow, alive and visible. Sable files the corrected report, first honest page in a rewritten archive. The emotional beat is bittersweet resolution: justice served, but both survivors pay the price of no longer being hidden.
